title: Aplysia Ganglia Preparation for Electrophysiological and Molecular Analyses of Single Neurons
protocol: Maintain Aplysia in the laboratory aquarium with circulating artificial seawater (ASW) at 16°C under 12:12 light:dark conditions.
Anesthetize animals by injecting a solution of 380 mM MgCl2 for 5-10 min, equivalent to 30-35% of the animal's body weight.
Identify the abdominal ganglion based on its position in the central nervous system.
Remove the abdominal ganglia and immediately store them in artificial seawater consisting of 450 mM NaCl, 10 mM KCl, 10 mM CaCl2, 55 mM MgCl2, 2.5 mM NaHCO3, and 10 mM HEPES (pH 7.4).
Incubate the abdominal ganglion for 30 min at 34°C ± 0.5 in a Petri dish with 0.1% protease (dispase) diluted in ASW.
Pin down the ganglia to the Sylgard Silicone base of a cell chamber after enzyme treatment.
Perfuse the ganglia with ASW at room temperature (18°C ± 2) at a flow rate of 150 μl/min.
Place the ganglion on top of a polycarbonate glass cylinder for illumination from below using a binocular stereomicroscope.
Remove the sheath from the ganglion carefully using forceps and microscissors.
Impale the neuron of interest with an intracellular sharp microelectrode filled with 3 M KCl solution, having resistance 10-15 MΩ.
Record neuronal activity at 10 kHz band pass using an intracellular recording system.
Process the recorded data using electrophysiology software such as Axograph.
Identify neurons L7, L11 or R15 and R2 based on their position for simultaneous recordings.
Apply drug of choice into the cell chamber by gentle pipetting.
Inject drug directly into the neurons if necessary.
Measure changes in membrane potential (MP) before, during, and after drug application.
Measure changes in action potential (AP) before, during, and after drug application.
Stop the perfusion of ASW and wash the ganglion with 100% ethanol.
Use fine forceps to remove individual neurons from the ganglion under a stereomicroscope.
Transfer isolated single neurons to an Eppendorf tube containing ice cold 500 μl RNA extraction reagent.
Store isolated single neurons in RNA extraction reagent at -80°C for future analysis.
Clean the working area and instruments with RNase deactivating agents.
Wear gloves while handling RNA and change gloves often during the process.
Use only RNase free plastics to handle RNAs.
Add 20% v/v of chloroform to Trizol, mix well by brief vortexing.
Place the tubes on a rotator for 10 min at 4°C.
Spin the Trizol-Chloroform mix at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4°C.
Collect the aqueous phase and transfer to a fresh tube.
Add sodium acetate solution (pH 5.5) to achieve a final concentration of 0.3 M.
Pipette 100 ng/ml of the coprecipitant GlycoBlue into the mixture.
Mix 2.5 volumes of 100% ethanol with the sample to precipitate RNA.
Incubate the samples at -80 °C overnight.
Spin the samples at 12,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant and wash the pellet with 850 μl of 75% ice-cold ethanol.
Centrifuge the samples at 12,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Air-dry the RNA pellet for 7-10 minutes.
Resuspend the dried RNA pellet in 10 μl of RNase-free water.
Determine the RNA concentration using a spectrophotometer.
Store RNA at -80 °C when not immediately used.
Amplify RNA from single neurons (one or two rounds) using a linear RNA amplification system.
Generate cDNA from amplified RNA using 1.0 μg of aRNA in a reverse transcription reaction.
Synthesize cDNA according to the manufacturer's protocol using a thermal cycler with settings: 5 min at 25 °C, 30 min at 42 °C, and 5 min at 85 °C.
Store synthesized cDNA at -20 °C for long-term storage after reverse transcription.
Select primers of 18-24 nucleotides that produce amplicons between 70-110 bp using primer design software.
Synthesize forward and reverse primer pairs for each gene of interest, with two to three sets per gene.
Standardize the primer set by qPCR to determine optimal Ct values and amplification curve shapes.
Monitor Ct values and amplification curves in qPCR to select primers with Ct values between 10-35 over 40 cycles.
Dilute cDNA to a final concentration of 5x with nuclease-free water for use in qPCR.
Add 8 μl of qPCR master mix to 2 μl of diluted cDNA.
Close the tubes after adding the master mix and primers.
Seal the plate tightly after pipetting.
Gently tap the tubes to mix contents thoroughly.
Spin down the plate at 1,500 rpm for 30 seconds.
